summary_paragraph: A woman with end-stage renal disease, mechanical mitral valve on anticoagulation, functioning pancreas transplant, and systolic heart failure was admitted for supratherapeutic INR of 10.6 and acute-on-chronic anemia, following transfer from an outside hospital. She had experienced mild chest pain attributed to demand ischemia from low hemoglobin, which resolved after blood transfusion and nitroglycerin. She received one unit of FFP and two units of packed red blood cells during her stay. INR initially dropped to 2.3 despite continued warfarin, prompting a short heparin bridge, which was discontinued once INR returned to therapeutic range. Warfarin was adjusted from 5 mg to 2.5 mg daily. She underwent scheduled hemodialysis, which helped manage acidosis and overall stability. The anemia was attributed to ongoing lower gastrointestinal oozing, with no acute intervention required. She remained stable, asymptomatic at discharge, and was sent home with services and close follow-up for INR monitoring.
problems: Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Heart valve replaced by other means
